rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (score 206.6, up from 51.7): the robot is still leaving the line, not oscillating. Every run ended off_track except 2 oval finishes. max_error sits at about 0.059 to 0.064 m, at the 0.06 m off-track limit, while steering_oscillation is moderate (0.20 to 0.33) and rms_error is small (0.017 to 0.027). Slalom averages 2.0 line-loss events, which fits the outer sensors at x = +/-0.03 m losing the 25 mm tape once the robot is offset by about 0.0175 m. Body width cannot widen the off-track limit here: max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.18/4 = 0.0575) is still 0.06. So the fix has to come from steering authority, damping and sensor coverage. Changes: (1) kp 3.5 to 4.0, a firmer correction so the robot pulls back toward the line sooner on bends (the error reaches the limit before it is corrected). (2) kd 0.6 to 0.9, more damping against the overshoot that the higher kp adds. (3) Sensor spread widened from +/-0.03 to +/-0.035 m, so the edge sensors keep seeing tape at larger offsets and line-loss events fall. Spacing is 0.0175 m, still under the 0.025 m tape width, so the centre sensors keep overlapping coverage. (4) base_speed kept at 1.3, since the oval finish time of 1.79 s leaves headroom but the s-bend failures show speed is not the first thing to cut. Mass, wheel geometry, ki and line_loss are unchanged to keep the comparison clean. Expected result: fewer off-track ends, line_loss_events under 1 on slalom, and s-bend progress above 0.5. Hypotheses: (a) if max_error still hits 0.06 on the s-bend, the robot needs more authority (kp near 5) or lower speed on the tight bends; (b) if steering_oscillation rises above about 0.5, kd or kp is too high and kd should go back toward 0.6; (c) if the oval still finishes only in a few seeds, the speed or kp mix is the limit and base_speed should be tested at 1.5 with the same gains. Next measurements: progress, completion, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort per track, so I can see whether the widened spread and higher kp are reducing edge losses and drift.
